title: Reconciliation receipt: accepted requirements → delivered code → canonical baseline
description: Receipt of ONE delivery step, in which code delivery and baseline (docs/spec/architecture) sync are two SEPARATE facts. The step may deliver code while the baseline is still pending; a receipt that claims a synced baseline without a commit and paths is false, not optimistic. Structural shape only — the honest-reading rules live in src/reconciliation/receipt.js (validate()), because a JSON Schema cannot say 'applied while a delta entry is not applied'.

plan.description: Who produced this receipt. The (plan_id, step_id) pair is the idempotency key: a replay of the same step emits the same receipt, never a second one.

requirements.description: The ACCEPTED requirements this delta is reconciled against, pinned to one revision. A newer revision makes an older receipt stale, not valid.

revision.description: revision marker of those requirements (@rev / commit sha)

code_delivery.description: FACT 1 — what happened to the CODE. Independent of the baseline: merged code with a pending baseline is a normal, allowed state.

refs.description: pr:<url> / sha:<sha> / commit:<sha> — empty or missing is allowed only with state=unknown

baseline.description: FACT 2 — what happened to the CANONICAL DOCS. Never inferred from code_delivery.

sync_kind.description: in_pr = docs rode the merged code PR; followup_pr = separate tracked docs PR after merge

paths.description: canonical files actually touched; REQUIRED (non-empty) for state=applied

delta.description: One entry per accepted requirement that the change touches. Per-requirement refs are the point: an unreferenced requirement is exactly the as-built story that drifts from reality.

requirement_ref.description: issue#135#L17 — where the accepted requirement is written

behavior_change.description: true = behaviour the user/system can observe; such a delta belongs in spec/contract, never in architecture only

deployed.description: true only when the change is observable in the running environment; deployed=false is a legitimate, honest value

evidence_refs.description: verification receipts, PRs, logs — non-empty; 'the file exists' is not evidence that a delta was applied

deferred.description: consciously out of scope — must be visible as a followup or a missing requirement, never as done

superseded_by.description: required for REMOVED unless removal_evidence is given

missing_requirements.description: Accepted requirements NOT reflected in the baseline. Empty is a claim the judge can check; absent means 'not collected'.

ref.description: issue#NN / doc path — a followup without a ref is a wish

conflicts.description: Baseline edited concurrently (parallel merge) or refused. A conflict is recorded, never overwritten and never reported as applied.

with.description: commit / branch / PR that touched the same baseline
